title.en: Countable and uncountable nouns; much, many, few, little
title.es: Contables e incontables; much, many, few, little

summary.en: **Countable** nouns can be counted (_one idea, two ideas_). **Uncountable** nouns cannot (_information, advice, money_) and have no plural. Use **many / few / a few** with countable nouns and **much / little / a little** with uncountable ones. **A lot of** works with both. **A few / a little** are positive (some); **few / little** are negative (not enough).
summary.es: Cuidado con palabras que en español son contables y en inglés no: information, advice, news, furniture, luggage, traffic, work.

form: Countable: **a/an**, numbers, plural **-s** (_a ticket, three tickets_)
Uncountable: no plural, no a/an; use **some**, **a piece of**, **a bit of** (_some advice_, _a piece of news_)
**many / few / a few** + plural countable; **much / little / a little** + uncountable
**much** and **many** are mostly used in questions and negatives; in positive sentences use **a lot of**

uses.text: **Countable**: _How **many** emails did you get?_ _There are **a few** seats left._
**Uncountable**: _How **much** time do we have?_ _We have **a little** time before the meeting._
**Positive or negative meaning**: _a few friends_ = some, enough; _few friends_ = hardly any. _A little money_ = some; _little money_ = hardly any.

note.en: Without a, few and little sound negative (not enough) and rather formal.
note.es: Few/little sin «a» expresan escasez: casi ninguno, muy poco.

uses.text: **A lot of / lots of** in positive sentences: _She has **a lot of** experience._ In negatives and questions, _much/many_ is more natural: _I don't have **much** free time._
**Both meanings**: some nouns change meaning, e.g. _paper_ (material) and _a paper_ (a newspaper or an essay); _time_ and _a time_.

mistakes.wrong: She gave me some advices about my CV.
mistakes.right: She gave me some advice about my CV.

why.en: Advice is uncountable, so it has no plural. Say a piece of advice.
why.es: Advice es incontable: no lleva -s ni a. «Un consejo» = a piece of advice.

why.en: News looks plural but is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
why.es: News acaba en -s pero es singular.

mistakes.wrong: I haven't got many money this month.
mistakes.right: I haven't got much money this month.

why.en: Money is uncountable, so use much, not many.
why.es: Money es incontable: much, no many.

mistakes.wrong: I have few time, so let's be quick.
mistakes.right: I have little time, so let's be quick.

why.en: Time is uncountable, so use little, not few.
why.es: Few va con contables; con incontables se usa little.

examples.en: There isn't much traffic on Sundays.
examples.es: No hay mucho tráfico los domingos.

examples.en: How many people are coming to the party?
I need some information about the course.
We've got a little time, so let's have a coffee.
Few students passed the exam, which surprised the teacher.
A few of my neighbours play in a band.
She gave me a useful piece of advice.
He has a lot of furniture but very little space.
Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
There are too many cars in the city centre.

practice.prompt: How ___ homework do you have tonight?

explanation.en: Homework is uncountable, so use much.

practice.prompt: There are only ___ tickets left, so book now.

explanation.en: Tickets are countable; a few means some, a small number.

practice.prompt: I'm afraid I've got very ___ patience with rude customers.

explanation.en: Patience is uncountable, and little means hardly any.

practice.prompt: The news about the strike ___ not good.

explanation.en: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
